audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer states the prerequisite on Lilting Lullaby. Both layers treat her ultimate as an unconditional sleep.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep." It only reaches targets already afflicted by Dream-Laden Bough. A Tahm Kench who has not been touched by one of her abilities recently cannot be slept at all. That single fact is the whole answer to her level-6 spike and it is absent, which is why the packet flags this matchup for zero cooldown-sequencing advice.
audit.corrected: Lilting Lullaby only sleeps enemies already carrying Dream Dust. Break contact and let the passive expire before she hits her ult window, and the 150s ultimate does nothing to you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry models Watch Out! Eep! as a bouncing projectile — "she bounces W off you", "her W bounce cycle", "chains Q into W bounces", and a tower-wall line: "her to misjudge a W bounce against your tower wall where the bounce arc clips the structure".
audit.why: Watch Out! Eep! is "Lillia deals damage in a nearby area, dealing heavy damage in the center" — a point-blank swing at 500 range with no travel and no bounce. The ability that rolls and interacts with walls is Swirlseed (E): "If it doesn't hit anything, it will continue rolling until it hits a wall or target." A player waiting to punish a bounced W off tower is watching for something that never happens, while the real roller is a different ability on a different cooldown.
audit.corrected: Watch Out! Eep! is a point-blank area swing (500 range, 14s at rank 1). Swirlseed is the roller (700 range, flat 12s) and it is the one that travels until it hits a wall or a target.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her Move Speed is attributed to the wrong abilities three times: spikes[1] "builds Move Speed off Lilting Lullaby and Dream-Laden Bough procs", whys[3] "Her Move Speed from Dream-Laden Bough procs", mid "enough Move Speed from Dream-Laden Bough procs".
audit.why: The Move Speed is on Blooming Blows: "Passively, Lillia gains stacking Move Speed when hitting enemies with spells." Dream-Laden Bough is the max-Health damage-over-time passive and Lilting Lullaby is the sleep. Getting the source wrong changes the counterplay — the speed comes from her landing spells on you, so the answer is to break contact, not to try to out-run or out-time an ult.
audit.corrected: Blooming Blows' passive stacks Move Speed every time one of her spells hits an enemy. Stop feeding it and the kite collapses.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json — Blooming Blows, Dream-Laden Bough, Lilting Lullaby

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full-layer cooldown model is keyed to Blooming Blows — focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, tldr, winCon, ahead, dosFull all say to track it and trade on its cooldown.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s. At rank 5 it is up every four seconds; there is no window to trade around and a player waiting for one waits forever. The cooldowns that are actually punishable are Swirlseed at a flat 12s at every rank — her only slow, per the kit's flag list — and Lilting Lullaby at 150/130/110s.
audit.corrected: Stop tracking Blooming Blows. Track Swirlseed (flat 12s, her only slow) for the walk-up window, and Lilting Lullaby (150s at rank 1) for the death window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json — cooldowns and kitFlags (slow: E only)

audit.whatIsWrong: content `late` claims that at item spikes "her full rotation barely dents you" and that grey health "cycles faster than her DOT damage".
audit.why: Dream-Laden Bough deals "additional max Health damage over time" and Blooming Blows deals "extra true damage on the edge" — _missing-interactions.json flags the second as resistances-invalidated. Percent-max-health damage scales up as Tahm Kench stacks Heartsteel, and true damage ignores the armour and MR he buys. So the item spike does not make her chip irrelevant; it makes his effective HP pool larger while her chip scales with it. Thick Skin still converts damage taken, which is why the lane is winnable, but the stated mechanism is wrong and will get a player killed walking into a rotation they think they out-scale.
audit.corrected: Dream-Laden Bough is max-Health damage and the outer ring of Blooming Blows is true damage — neither HP nor resistances scale you out of her chip. What saves you is Thick Skin conversion and not being in Dream Dust when the ult goes out.

audit.whatIsWrong: content `mid`, `late` and whys[4] build the level-6 answer on "Abyssal Voyage".
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage — W is Abyssal Dive, R is Devour. whys[4] in particular makes it the entire reason level 6 flattens to Skill, which leaves that stage with no real justification once the ability is removed. The genuine reason level 6 evens out is the Dream Dust prerequisite on her ultimate.
audit.corrected: Level 6 evens out because Lilting Lullaby cannot touch a target that is not already dusted, not because of a global relocate that does not exist.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2], whys[6], spikes[3] and full tradeGood/dosFull all chain the Tongue Lash stun into Devour.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at 3 stacks stuns and consumes the stacks; Devour requires three stacks. Against the fastest kiter in the matchup pool, spending your stacks on a short stun instead of a multi-second removal is the worse half of a choice the entry does not know it is making.
audit.corrected: Three stacks, one purchase: take Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

edits.before: At level 1 this is a neutral feeling lane — your Tongue Lash range lets you tag her for passive stacks but Lillia's passive DOT starts burning you immediately any time her W or Q clips you. Farm at max Tongue Lash range and do not chase into her kite circle. The moment you step up to trade she bounces W and retreats, leaving the DOT ticking while you sit too far from her to land a second Q for stacks. At level 2 she starts chaining Q into W more confidently and her DOT cycle will shave chunks off your health faster than your grey health regenerates if she keeps landing small hits — respect this, play for CS, and bank your 3 stacks for a rare moment she steps into a bush or onto a short wave.
edits.after: At level 1 this is a neutral feeling lane — Tongue Lash reaches 900 and lets you tag her for stacks, but Dream-Laden Bough starts burning max-Health damage the instant Blooming Blows or Watch Out! Eep! clips you. Farm at max Tongue Lash range and do not chase into her kite circle. She swings and steps back out, leaving the Dream Dust ticking while you sit too far away to land a second Q for stacks. At level 2 her chip shaves chunks off you faster than grey health regenerates — respect it, play for CS, and bank your 3 stacks for a moment she steps into a bush, or for the twelve seconds after Swirlseed, which is the only slow she has.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Lillia's clearest advantage: she has enough Move Speed from Dream-Laden Bough procs and item starts to orbit you indefinitely, your Tongue Lash is predictable on a straight axis, and she never commits to a melee window you can punish with Devour. Do not burn Flash chasing — she wins that exchange. Hug your tower, keep your Thick Skin grey health high by activating it as soon as you leave her DOT, and look for her to misjudge a W bounce against your tower wall where the bounce arc clips the structure. At level 6 the power balance genuinely levels out: you have Abyssal Voyage to relocate and she cannot sleep you into a kill if you are near tower, but she still beats you in the open field — treat it as Skill until your first item arrives.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Lillia's clearest advantage: Blooming Blows' passive stacks Move Speed every time one of her spells touches you, so she orbits indefinitely, your Tongue Lash is predictable on a straight axis, and she never commits to a window you can punish with Devour. Do not burn Flash chasing — she wins that exchange. Hug your tower, activate Thick Skin as soon as you leave her chip, and play the twelve seconds after a missed Swirlseed, which is flat at every rank. At level 6 the balance levels out for one reason worth memorising: Lilting Lullaby only sleeps enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so if you are clean when she casts it, it does nothing at all to you and the 150s is wasted.

edits.before: Once Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis comes online you stop being a passive-DOT target and become an attrition wall: her full rotation barely dents you and Thick Skin converts the remaining grey health into a shield that cycles on every re-engage she attempts. At 2+ items you simply walk at her — she cannot burst a 4-5k health Tahm Kench before Tongue Lash lands a stun and Devour removes her from the fight. Your Abyssal Voyage also threatens to port into her team and Devour her during an R sleep setup before it ever resolves. Teamfights are yours: you peel your carry, flash-stun any Lillia who dives, and let your grey health eat the DOT damage she was counting on.
edits.after: Once Heartsteel comes online Thick Skin converts her chip into a shield that cycles on every re-engage, but do not read that as immunity: Dream-Laden Bough is max-Health damage and the edge of Blooming Blows is true damage, so neither the HP nor the resistances you buy scale you out of them. At 2+ items you can still simply walk at her — she cannot burst a 4-5k Tahm Kench before three stacks turn into Devour, and the stun would only consume those same stacks. Teamfights are yours: peel your carry, and shed Dream Dust before she ults, because Lilting Lullaby cannot sleep what it has not already dusted.

notes: Lillia's full layer refers to her as male throughout — "Q-stun when his answer is down", "If he snowballs", "Devour deletes him from the fight", breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late. I fixed the pronoun only where I was already rewriting the string for a factual reason (tradeGood); breakdown.trading, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, dosFull[1].d and the report[] copies still say "him"/"his". Worth a mechanical sweep rather than nine hand edits. Also note the packet's suspectName on "Laden Bough" is a false positive — the string in spikes[1] is correctly spelled "Dream-Laden Bough"; the real defect in that sentence is that Dream-Laden Bough and Lilting Lullaby are credited with Move Speed that belongs to Blooming Blows.
